items.title: MSF warns of worsening malnutrition crisis among displaced children in Somalia
items.description: The United Nations says more than 500,000 Somalis were displaced during the first three months of this year, with drought responsible for nine out of ten displacements.

items.title: What investing in Africa means to Aliko Dangote, By Ehi Braimah
items.description: When conversations turn to investment in Africa, one name consistently dominates the discussion: Aliko Dangote. Over the past four decades, the Nigerian industrialist has become more than Africa’s richest businessman – he has emerged as one of the continent’s most influential advocates for industrialisation, value addition and economic self-reliance. His investments tell a story that […] The post What investing in Africa means to Aliko Dangote, By Ehi Braimah appeared first on Premium Times Nigeria .

items.title: Civil society groups warn against Congo referendum
items.description: In the Democratic Republic of Congo, 65 civil society organisations are urging President Félix Tshisekedi to abandon plans for a constitutional referendum.

items.title: Colombia: Bogota's search for survivors continues
items.description: The search for survivors continues in Colombia, more than 48 hours after a 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck the country. More than 200 people have been confirmed dead, while more than 2,000 are reported missing. The new president, Abelardo de la Espriella, has declared a state of emergency, as many people remain without clean drinking water or electricity and several major highways are still closed. Carys Garland’s report begins with the dramatic rescue of a man from the wreckage of his home.

items.title: Zambia heads to polls with President Hichilema expected to win second term
items.description: Zambians vote Thursday in a general election widely expected to give President Hakainde Hichilema a second term, as his economic record faces a test from voters frustrated by the cost of living and opposition parties seek to capitalise on discontent despite deep divisions.

items.title: Adopted Indian women find 'missing piece' when DNA test reveals they are sisters
items.description: Growing up, neither was aware that they had a sister. Then, as teenagers ‌in 1996, while living just 100 miles (130 km) apart, they ‌crossed ⁠paths at a gathering for adopted children and felt ⁠an unusually strong connection

items.title: Colombia: Woman rescued from under earthquake debris after 36 hours
items.description: 🇨🇴 A woman trapped under the debris of a collapsed hotel in Pereira, #Colombia, was rescued on Tuesday after spending 36 hours under the rubble. Search and rescue operations are still underway in the country's coffee-growing Chocó region which was at the epîcentre of a 7.4 magnitude #earthquake on Monday.

items.title: Trump administration plans to give ICE officers electric-shock gloves
items.description: US Homeland Security is expected to buy up to $20m in gloves amid criticism of the president's immigration crackdown.

items.title: Nissan management shake-up plans reported as sharks circle
items.description: Nissan is considering a change in leadership following poor results and the failure of a proposed merger with Honda, according to a report citing unnamed sources.

items.title: U.S. lawmaker voices concern on FCRA amendments; says could hit bilateral ties with India
items.description: U.S. Congressman Riley Moore said the amendments to FCRA would permit the Indian government to takeover churches and religious charities and would amount to “clear attack against Christians”

items.title: Tigray rebels accuse Ethiopia of drone strikes amid fears of renewed war
items.description: Tigray rebel authorities have accused Ethiopia’s federal government of carrying out deadly drone strikes in the region, raising fears of a renewed conflict nearly four years after a peace deal ended a devastating two-year war.

items.description: The designation of PCC and CV serves to expand Washington’s reach into the country’s politics and security.

items.description: A postcard of environmental disaster at first sight: hundreds of trawlers with lights blazing navigating at the edge of Argentine waters. items.title: When extreme heat threatens Europe's nuclear power
items.description: Warm rivers and low water levels are forcing nuclear power plants to reduce output across Europe. Over a year, the losses are minimal, but on critical days the loss of power has consequences for grids and prices.

items.title: Parts of Spain plunged into darkness as eclipse moves across Europe
items.description: Parts of Spain were briefly plunged into darkness on Wednesday as a solar eclipse that began in Iceland and the Arctic progressed across the continent. It was the first total eclipse to be seen from mainland Europe in two decades. Read our blog to see how the event unfolded.

items.title: Making sense of Trump's executive order on US vaccinations
items.description: President Donald Trump and his Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. have long tried to reduce the number of vaccinations available to the US public and even farm animals. The latest move in context.

items.description: The former head of Catholic Schools NSW says he did seek financial support from federal Opposition Leader Angus Taylor, but denied it was for a right-wing Liberal factional group at the centre of a corruption probe.

items.title: Moment Cali hospital collapses after powerful Colombia earthquake

items.title: Colombia declares three days of mourning as search for quake survivors continues
items.description: Colombia on Wednesday declared three days of mourning after a 7.4-magnitude earthquake killed more than 200 people in the west of the country. Monday's quake was the strongest to hit Colombia this century, and the search for survivors under the rubble is ongoing.

items.title: Ballarat man accused of raping teenager at neighbour's home
items.description: A teenager asked Ballarat man Lachlan Young what his girlfriend would think about claims that he raped her in 2024, a Victorian court has heard.

items.title: EU waste packaging rules: Why small businesses are worried
items.description: The EU has introduced new rules targeting packaging waste and "forever chemicals." Although the changes will be phased in slowly, some small sellers have already paused shipments due to the additional red tape.

items.title: Moroccan authorities say they have beefed up security at Ceuta border
items.description: The annoucement comes as calls resurfaced on social media for mass crossings into the Spanish enclave in North Africa.

items.title: Syrians celebrate landmark verdict as court sentences Bashar Assad to death in absentia
items.description: Bashar and Maher Assad remain in Russia after fleeing Syria following the collapse of their government. Syria's new authorities have called on Moscow to extradite them to face justice.

items.title: Ceuta migrant crisis deepens as leader calls for detention centre
items.description: Spain is facing mounting pressure over the migrant crisis in Ceuta after tens of thousands crossed from Morocco last month. The enclave’s leader is calling for a detention centre, while Madrid insists border controls and security measures remain firmly in place.

items.title: Hichilema rallies thousands as Zambia heads to presidential vote
items.description: Tens of thousands of supporters gathered in Lusaka for President Hakainde Hichilema’s final campaign rally ahead of Thursday’s election, as the incumbent seeks a second term amid concerns over jobs, living costs and allegations of opposition intimidation.
